### Working Papers

***On P-Zombies, Synaptogenesis, and Dopaminergic Degeneration*** \[PDF later\] *(2026--Present)*  
*Philosophy. Tags: Chalmers, 1996 ; Multiple Realizability ; Action ; Parkinson's Disease*  
[**Background**]{.underline}: Reading Chalmers is *sometimes* eyebrow-raising and *always* thought-provoking.  
[**Motivating**]{.underline}: There's not much philosophical zombie discussion relating to trauma and this continuation was immediately interesting to me; as an innocent hobbyist I do not hold a side in the consciousness debate (yet) -- I am seeing where my wandering mind takes me.

***Colliders: Lessons from Graduate Economics Enrollment*** \[PDF soon/data on request\] *(2022--Present)*  
*Economics. Tags: Sapienza, 2009 ; Decision-making ; Berkson's Paradox*  
[**Background**]{.underline}: While merrily deriving matrix calculus beta-hats and working through Gauss-Markov as a sophomore, I realized I do not actually know anything about Economics PhD admissions as an immigrant \& a CC transfer.  
[**Motivating**]{.underline}: The only reasonable thing was to use departmental websites, LinkedIn, and the internet to compile a list of 547 2021-22 enrollees into "better" PhD programs and see what is up. Of course, not all admits choose to enroll, and I only had enrollment data.  
[**Interpreting**]{.underline}: Precisely this friction point acts as a logistic mechanism revealing a significant result *(N=314, p=0.02247, CI=positive)* and invites digging deeper into econometric, psychological, and behavioral considerations -- to which I gladly oblige.
